examples.ko: 그 사건은 권력자의 비호 속에서 오랫동안 숨겨졌어요.
examples.en: That incident stayed hidden for a long time under a powerful person's protection.

examples.ko: 기자가 누구의 비호를 받았는지 계속 물었어요.
examples.en: The reporter kept asking whose protection he had received.

examples.ko: 높은 사람의 비호가 없으면 이런 일은 불가능해요.
examples.en: Without a high-ranking person's backing, this would be impossible.

examples.ko: 그는 상사의 비호 아래 계속 승진했어요.
examples.en: He kept getting promoted under his boss's patronage.

examples.ko: 부모의 비호만 믿고 노력하지 않으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You can't just rely on your parents' protection and not make any effort.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 정치인의 비호 덕분에 큰 계약을 땄어요.
examples.en: That company won a big contract thanks to a politician's backing.

explain: 힘 있는 사람이 누군가의 잘못을 감싸 주고 지켜 줄 때 쓰는 말이라서, 주로 안 좋은 뉴스에 나와요. '비호를 받다', '비호 아래'처럼 써요. 일상에서는 '감싸 주다', '편들어 주다'라고 말해요.

phrases.example: 그는 높은 사람의 비호를 받고 있다는 소문이 있어요.
phrases.en: There are rumors that he is being protected by someone powerful.
phrases.nuance_ko: '받다'와 함께 써서 힘 있는 사람이 잘못을 감싸 준다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 받다, it means a powerful person is covering for someone's wrongdoing.

phrases.en: Under the protection of those in power, the wrongdoing continued.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누구의 보호 속에서 어떤 일이 일어났는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say under whose cover something happened.

phrases.example: 잘못한 사람을 계속 감싸 주면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: You shouldn't keep covering for someone who did wrong.
phrases.nuance_ko: '비호'를 일상에서 쉽게 말할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the easy everyday way to say what 비호 means.

explain_en: It is used when someone powerful shields another person, often covering up their faults, so it mostly appears in negative news. It is used in forms like '비호를 받다' and '비호 아래'. In daily talk people say '감싸 주다' or '편들어 주다'.

t90.ax: He kept getting promoted under his boss's patronage.

en: to be conned; to be duped; to be swindled

examples.en: I got scammed in a secondhand deal.
My grandmother almost got scammed over the phone.
I want to get back the money I was scammed out of.
I heard that my friend got swindled.
Be careful not to get scammed at online shops.

examples.ko: 사기당하고 나서 아무도 못 믿게 됐어요.
examples.en: After being swindled, I couldn't trust anyone.

explain: 속인 사람은 '사기를 치다'라고 하고, 당한 사람은 '사기당하다'라고 해요. 가볍게 '속았다'고도 하는데, 돈을 잃는 큰 일이면 '사기당했다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I was scammed on the internet.
phrases.nuance_ko: '사기당하다'를 두 말로 나눈 형태로, 뜻은 같아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The same meaning as 사기당하다, split into two words.

phrases.en: I was fooled by my friend's words and lost money.
phrases.nuance_ko: '사기당하다'보다 가볍고, 속아 넘어갔다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Lighter than 사기당하다; it means being fooled or tricked.

phrases.en: Be careful so you don't get scammed.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지 않게'를 붙여서 조심하라고 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used with -지 않게 to give a warning.
phrases.en_equiv: so as not to be scammed

explain_en: The scammer 'does' it ('사기를 치다'); the victim says '사기당하다'. People also say '속았다' casually, but when real money is lost, '사기당했다' sounds more natural.

examples.en: He is on trial for fraud.

examples.ko: 사기죄가 인정되면 징역형을 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If fraud is established, he could get a prison sentence.
Used-goods trading scams also count as fraud.
The police investigated him on suspicion of fraud.
A rumor spread that my friend had committed fraud.
I heard that person has a fraud record.

explain: '사기를 치다'는 일상에서 쓰는 말이고, '사기죄'는 뉴스나 재판 이야기에서 법적인 죄를 말할 때 써요. '사기가 오르다'의 '사기'는 기운을 뜻하는 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: The victim filed a fraud complaint against him.
phrases.nuance_ko: 법적으로 죄를 물을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when legally accusing someone of the crime.

phrases.en: The fraud charge was upheld at the trial.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재판에서 죄가 확정되는 상황에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a court recognizes the crime.

phrases.en: Taking money through lies counts as fraud.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 행동이 법적으로 사기가 되는지 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to explain that an act legally counts as fraud.

explain_en: '사기를 치다' is the everyday phrase, while '사기죄' is used in the news and court talk for the legal crime. The '사기' in '사기가 오르다' (morale rises) is a different word meaning spirit.

examples.ko: 외국 것이라면 무조건 좋다고 하는 건 사대주의예요.
examples.en: Saying that anything foreign is automatically good is flunkyism.

examples.ko: 역사 시간에 조선 시대 사대주의에 대해 배웠어요.
examples.en: In history class, we learned about flunkyism in the Joseon period.

examples.ko: 그 글은 사대주의 때문에 우리 문화를 낮춰 본다고 비판해요.
examples.en: That article criticizes looking down on our own culture because of flunkyism.

examples.ko: 사대주의에서 벗어나 스스로 판단하는 게 중요해요.
examples.en: It is important to break free from flunkyism and judge for yourself.

examples.ko: 큰 나라만 따르는 사대주의가 문제라고 생각해요.
examples.en: I think the flunkyism of only following big countries is the problem.

examples.ko: 사대주의적인 생각은 버려야 한다고 선생님이 말씀하셨어요.
examples.en: My teacher said we should get rid of flunkyist thinking.

explain: 대부분 비판하거나 부정적으로 말할 때 써요. 역사 수업에서는 큰 나라를 섬기는 외교 태도를, 일상에서는 외국 것을 무조건 높이는 태도를 말해요. 남에게 쓰면 심한 말이 될 수 있으니 조심해요.

phrases.example: 외국 브랜드만 좋아하면 사대주의에 빠진 거라고 말하는 사람도 있어요.
phrases.en: Some people say that liking only foreign brands is falling into flunkyism.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그런 태도에 깊이 빠진 사람을 비판할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to criticize someone deeply caught up in that attitude.

phrases.en: That kind of flunkyist thinking has to change.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생각이나 태도를 꾸밀 때 '-적인'을 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-적인' to describe a way of thinking or attitude.

phrases.en: I studied the flunkyist diplomacy of the Joseon period.
phrases.nuance_ko: 역사 수업에서 외교 태도를 설명할 때 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears in history class when explaining diplomatic attitudes.

explain_en: It is mostly used critically. In history class it refers to a diplomatic stance of serving a bigger power, and in daily life to automatically elevating anything foreign. It can sound harsh when aimed at a person, so be careful.

en: social evil; social ill; social problem

examples.ko: 부정부패는 반드시 없애야 할 사회악이라고 생각해요.
examples.en: I think corruption is a social evil that must be eliminated.

examples.ko: 도박 중독을 사회악으로 보는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people see gambling addiction as a social evil.

examples.ko: 사회악을 줄이려면 정부와 시민이 함께 노력해야 해요.
examples.en: To reduce social evils, the government and citizens must work together.

examples.ko: 거짓 정보도 큰 사회악이 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: False information can also become a major social evil.
Citizens' anger toward social evils has grown.

examples.ko: 사기 범죄는 선량한 사람들을 괴롭히는 사회악이에요.
examples.en: Fraud is a social evil that torments good people.

explain: '사회 문제'는 중립적인 말이지만, '사회악'은 그 현상을 강하게 비난하는 느낌이에요. 연설이나 신문 글, 토론에서 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '큰 문제'라고 말하는 경우가 더 많아요.

phrases.en: The police work to get rid of social evils.
phrases.nuance_ko: 범죄나 부패 같은 큰 문제를 없앤다고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about eliminating big problems like crime or corruption.

phrases.en: Indifference can also become a social evil.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일이 사회에 해로운 것으로 번진다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something grows into a harmful force in society.

phrases.en: Garbage is a big social problem.
phrases.nuance_ko: '사회악'보다 덜 강하고 일상에서 더 자주 쓰는 중립적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more neutral and everyday word that is milder than 사회악.

explain_en: '사회 문제' (social problem) is neutral, but '사회악' strongly condemns the phenomenon. It often appears in speeches, newspaper writing and debates. In everyday talk people more often just say '큰 문제' (a big problem).

en: to be murdered; to be killed

examples.en: In the novel, a rich man is murdered.
The man was murdered in front of his house.
The family of the murdered person is grieving.
The criminal fled before the victim was murdered.
He was found two days after being murdered.
The police saved a person who was nearly murdered.

explain: '죽임을 당하다'와 같은 뜻이지만 뉴스·수사 기사에서는 '살해되다'를 써요. 사고나 병으로 죽은 경우에는 쓰지 않고, 누군가가 일부러 죽였을 때만 써요. 죽인 쪽 말은 '살해하다'예요.

phrases.en: In that novel, the main character's friend is murdered.
phrases.nuance_ko: 당하는 쪽의 입장을 더 느끼게 하는 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This similar word puts more feeling on the victim's side.

phrases.example: 한 남자가 집에서 살해된 채 발견됐어요.
phrases.en: A man was found murdered at home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 자주 듣는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This pairing is often heard in the news.

phrases.example: 그 살해 사건은 아직 풀리지 않았어요.
phrases.en: That murder case hasn't been solved yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 일부러 죽은 사건을 부르는 명사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: This noun names a case in which someone was deliberately killed.

explain_en: It means the same as '죽임을 당하다', but news and investigation reports use '살해되다'. It is not used for deaths by accident or illness, only when someone killed on purpose. The killer's side uses '살해하다'.

p.n: 피살되다 is even more like a news headline.

examples.ko: 실종됐던 등산객의 생환 소식에 가족들이 눈물을 흘렸어요.
examples.en: The family cried at the news that the missing hiker had returned alive.

examples.ko: 구조대원들은 마지막까지 생환을 기대하며 수색을 이어 갔어요.
examples.en: The rescuers continued the search, hoping for survivors until the very end.

examples.ko: 매몰됐던 광부 두 명이 열흘 만에 생환에 성공했어요.
examples.en: Two buried miners made it out alive after ten days.
The survivors who came back all looked healthy.

examples.ko: 기적 같은 생환이라며 뉴스마다 크게 보도했어요.
examples.en: Every news outlet reported it widely as a miraculous return alive.

examples.ko: 모두가 포기했을 때 일어난 생환이라서 더 감동적이었어요.
examples.en: It was a return alive that happened when everyone had given up, so it was even more moving.

explain: 뉴스나 기사에서 조난이나 재난 뒤에 나오는 딱딱한 말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '살아서 돌아오다'라고 풀어서 말해요.

phrases.en: The family was delighted to hear the news of the safe return.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 자주 쓰는 가장 대표적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most typical pairing, often seen in the news.

phrases.en: The families are eagerly waiting for them to come back alive.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사고가 난 사람이 살아 돌아오기를 바랄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when hoping an endangered person comes back alive.
phrases.en_equiv: to wait for one's safe return

phrases.en: People celebrated the rescued sailor's safe return.
phrases.nuance_ko: 살아 돌아온 것을 함께 기뻐할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when celebrating someone's survival and return.

explain_en: It is a stiff word that shows up in news reports after accidents, disasters or disappearances. In daily conversation people spell it out as '살아서 돌아오다'.

examples.ko: 경찰은 이번 주 안에 사건 송치를 마칠 계획이에요.
examples.en: The police plan to finish forwarding the case within this week.
After the transfer, the prosecution takes over the case.
The transfer was delayed, so the announcement of results was postponed too.
I saw the news about the case being sent to the prosecution.
I heard whether it will be forwarded will be decided next week.
The paperwork procedure for forwarding is more complicated than I thought.

explain: 일상에서 물건을 '보내다'처럼 쓰지 않고, 경찰이 수사한 사건을 검찰로 넘길 때 주로 써요. 뉴스에서 '검찰 송치'라는 말로 자주 볼 수 있어요.

phrases.en: It was decided that the case would be referred to the prosecutors.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 '송치'와 가장 자주 함께 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing with 송치 in the news.

phrases.en: The police finished the referral yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 송치 절차가 끝났다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say the referral process is complete.

phrases.example: 송치 전에 조사를 한 번 더 해요.
phrases.en: They do one more investigation before the referral.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사건을 넘기기 전 단계를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the stage before the case is handed over.

explain_en: It is not used like '보내다' for everyday items; it is mainly used when the police pass an investigated case on to the prosecution. You often see it in the news as '검찰 송치'.

t90.ax: After the transfer, the prosecution takes over the case.

en: repatriation; sending back to one's home country

examples.en: The government decided to send the illegal entrants back to their home country.

examples.ko: 포로 송환 문제로 두 나라가 회의를 열었어요.
examples.en: The two countries held a meeting over the issue of returning prisoners of war.
The families are worried because the repatriation has been delayed.
We prepared the documents needed to send the criminal back.
Forced repatriation is also connected to human rights issues.

examples.ko: 조사가 끝나면 곧바로 송환으로 이어질 거예요.
examples.en: Once the investigation ends, it will lead straight to repatriation.

explain: 송환은 주로 외교·재판 뉴스에서 쓰고, 본인 뜻과 상관없이 보낸다는 느낌이 있어요. 물건을 돌려보낼 때는 '반송'이라고 해요. '귀국'은 스스로 돌아가는 거라서 달라요.

phrases.en: The government temporarily halted forced repatriation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 본인 뜻과 상관없이 억지로 돌려보내는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to sending someone back against their will.

phrases.en: That country demanded the return of the criminal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 나라에 있는 사람을 돌려보내라고 요구할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when demanding that a person in another country be sent back.

phrases.example: 송환 절차는 몇 달이 걸릴 수 있어요.
phrases.en: The repatriation process can take several months.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 돌려보내기까지 거쳐야 하는 순서를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The steps that must be completed before someone is sent back.

explain_en: 송환 appears mainly in diplomatic and legal news and suggests being sent back regardless of one's own wishes. For sending goods back, 반송 is used. 귀국 is different because the person returns by their own choice.

examples.en: The illegal resident was sent back to their home country.

examples.ko: 해외로 달아난 범인이 한국으로 송환될 예정이에요.
examples.en: The criminal who fled abroad is scheduled to be sent back to Korea.

examples.ko: 포로들이 모두 고향으로 송환되고 나서야 안심했어요.
examples.en: I only felt relieved after all the prisoners had been sent back home.
The safety of the people being sent back is the most important thing.
Once the remains are returned home, we will hold the funeral.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 부상으로 중간에 송환된 적이 있어요.
examples.en: That athlete was once sent home partway through because of an injury.

explain: 송환되다는 자기 뜻과 상관없이 돌려보내질 때 써서 '돌아가다'와 달라요. '한국으로 송환되다'처럼 '으로'로 도착지를 붙여요. 말할 때는 '송환돼요', '송환됐어요'로 줄여요.

phrases.en: He was forcibly sent back to his home country.
phrases.nuance_ko: 본인이 원하지 않았다는 점을 분명히 말할 때 '강제로'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '강제로' to make clear it was against the person's will.

phrases.en: Without documents, you could be sent back.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그럴 가능성이 있다고 경고할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to warn that this is a possibility.

phrases.en: He hasn't been sent back yet because of the trial.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 돌려보내지지 않았다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say that someone hasn't been sent back yet.

explain_en: 송환되다 is used when someone is sent back regardless of their own wishes, so it differs from 돌아가다. The destination is marked with 으로, as in 한국으로 송환되다. In speech it contracts to 송환돼요 or 송환됐어요.

en: being secretly; being covertly; being implicitly

examples.en: That plan was being carried out secretly.

examples.ko: 암암리에 소문이 퍼져서 모두 알고 있었어요.
examples.en: The rumor spread quietly, and everyone already knew.

examples.ko: 두 회사가 암암리에 약속을 했다고 해요.
examples.en: They say the two companies made a secret agreement.

examples.ko: 학생들은 암암리에 서로 눈치를 보고 있어요.
examples.en: The students are quietly watching each other's reactions.
That kind of rule is being followed without anyone saying so.
There was someone who helped behind the scenes.

explain: 거의 항상 '암암리에' 형태로 쓰고, 공개하지 않고 조용히 또는 말없이 이루어지는 일에 써요. '몰래'보다 딱딱해서 뉴스나 글에 더 어울려요. 나쁜 일뿐 아니라 말없이 모두가 따르는 규칙에도 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: The merger talks are proceeding quietly behind the scenes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공개하지 않고 조용히 일이 이어진다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means something goes on quietly without being made public.

phrases.en: The news spread quietly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공식 발표 없이 사람들 사이에 조용히 알려진다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it becomes known among people without an official announcement.

phrases.example: 그 맛집은 암암리에 알려져서 줄이 길어요.
phrases.en: That restaurant became known quietly, and now the line is long.
phrases.nuance_ko: 광고 없이 조용히 알려졌다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the sense of becoming known quietly without advertising.

explain_en: It is almost always used in the form '암암리에', for things done quietly or without being openly stated. It is stiffer than '몰래', so it fits the news and writing better. It can describe not only secret wrongdoing but also unspoken rules everyone follows.

en: to be plundered; to be pillaged; to be looted

examples.en: Many villages were plundered during the war.
The shop was looted, so there's nothing left.
There was an incident where the museum's treasures were looted.
They say this cultural property was taken by force long ago.
The villagers stood guard so that nothing would be plundered.
The house was looted and burned down.

explain: '도둑맞다'는 몰래 훔쳐 간 경우이고, '약탈당하다'는 힘이나 폭력으로 빼앗긴 경우예요. 전쟁이나 역사 이야기에서 많이 써요. 하는 쪽을 말하면 '약탈하다'예요.

phrases.en: During the war, people had their property taken.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서도 쓰는 쉬운 말로, 힘으로 뺏긴다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier everyday word meaning to have something taken by force.

phrases.en: The looted cultural assets were returned.
phrases.nuance_ko: 역사 이야기에서 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing in talk about history.

phrases.en: During the war, the village almost got plundered.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄹ 뻔하다'를 붙이면 거의 그럴 뻔했지만 실제로는 아니었다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-ㄹ 뻔하다' means it almost happened but did not.

explain_en: 도둑맞다 is for things stolen secretly; 약탈당하다 is for things taken by force or violence, mostly in talk of war and history. The side doing it is 약탈하다.

en: to be suppressed; to be oppressed

examples.en: In a society where freedom is suppressed, speaking up is hard.

examples.ko: 억압된 감정은 언젠가 다른 모습으로 나타나요.
examples.en: Suppressed emotions show up in another form someday.
When opinions are suppressed, ideas stop coming.
In those days, women's rights were suppressed.
The pent-up anger burst out all at once.
The more expression is suppressed, the more the discontent grows.

explain: 억압되다는 자유, 감정, 의견, 권리가 힘에 눌려 드러나지 못할 때 써요. 사회 이야기에도, 마음 이야기('억압된 감정')에도 모두 써요. 누르는 쪽은 '억압하다'예요. 스스로 참는 것은 '참다'를 써요.

phrases.en: Suppressed emotions are not good for your health.
phrases.nuance_ko: '억압되다'를 명사 앞에 붙이는 활용형이에요. 마음속에 눌려 있는 감정을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form before a noun, describing feelings pushed down inside.

phrases.example: 그 시대 사람들은 말할 자유가 없이 억압받았어요.
phrases.en: People of that era were oppressed, with no freedom to speak.
phrases.nuance_ko: '억압되다'와 비슷하고, 누군가에게 눌림을 당했다는 느낌이 더 분명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 억압되다 but makes clearer that someone pressed you down.

phrases.example: 그 나라에서는 표현의 자유가 억압되어 있어요.
phrases.en: In that country, freedom of expression is suppressed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금도 눌려 있는 상태를 말할 때 쓰는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form used to describe a state that is still ongoing.

explain_en: 억압되다 is used when freedom, emotions, opinions or rights are pressed down and cannot show. It works for society and for the mind, as in 억압된 감정. The pressing side is 억압하다. Holding something back by yourself is 참다.

t90.ax: The pent-up anger burst out all at once.

en: to be connected; to be linked

examples.ko: 이 앱은 은행 계좌와 연계되어 있어요.
examples.en: This app is linked to a bank account.

examples.ko: 학교 수업이 실제 일과 연계되면 더 재미있어요.
examples.en: Classes are more fun when they are tied to real work.

examples.ko: 두 사건이 서로 연계된 것 같아요.
examples.en: The two incidents seem to be connected.
Services that link up with transit cards are increasing.
This program is tied to job placement.

examples.ko: 카페 앱과 연계되고 나서 주문이 편해졌어요.
examples.en: Ordering got easier after it was linked to the cafe's app.

explain: 서비스·제도·수업·정보처럼 서로 다른 것이 이어져 함께 움직일 때 써요. 사람 사이의 관계에는 잘 안 써요. '관련되다'는 그냥 관계가 있다는 느낌이고, '연계되다'는 실제로 이어져 작동한다는 느낌이 강해요. 광고와 안내문에서 많이 봐요.

phrases.en: I took part in a program linked with the library.
phrases.nuance_ko: '연계된'은 명사 앞에서 이어진 것을 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: '연계된' modifies a noun that is linked to something.

phrases.en: The two systems are linked with each other.
phrases.nuance_ko: '서로'를 넣으면 양쪽이 함께 움직인다는 뜻이 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '서로' makes clear that both sides work together.
phrases.en_equiv: to be linked with each other

phrases.example: 이 계정은 휴대폰 번호와 연결되어 있어요.
phrases.en: This account is connected to my phone number.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 쉽고 넓게 쓰는 말이라서 길, 전화, 계정에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier and broader, also used for roads, calls, and accounts.

explain_en: It is used when separate things such as services, systems, classes or information are tied together and work as one. It is rarely used for relationships between people. 관련되다 only means there is some relation; 연계되다 stresses that things are actually connected and working together. You see it a lot in ads and notices.

dis.h: be tied in cooperation, like programs
gh: get connected to a website or network

p.s: 이 수업은 회사 일과 연계돼 있어요.
p.o: 이 수업은 회사 일과 연결돼 있어요.
p.n: 연결되다 only says they are linked; 연계되다 means they are set up to work together.

t90.ax: This app is linked to a bank account.
